questions: Did line_loss_events drop to 0 on the s-bend and slalom with the outer sensors at +/-0.060 m?
Did max_error fall below 0.06 m, and on which track did the first off-track event occur?
Did the 7-sensor array raise steering_oscillation noticeably compared with the 5-sensor version in iteration 1?
If line loss is zero but max_error still reaches 0.06 m, is the robot short of turn authority on the tightest bend?

intent: Test whether line loss at large offsets is the sole cause of off-track failure. Changes from iteration 1: outer sensors moved from x = +/-0.036 m to +/-0.060 m, sensor count raised from 5 to 7 at 20 mm spacing to keep resolution, footprint kept at 16 mm, y kept at 0.03 m, wheel_track and mass kept unchanged. Expected result: line_loss_events 0, max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend, and a finish on at least some seeds. If line loss is still 1 or more, the sensing reach is not the cause and the next lever is turn authority.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that a 72 mm span (outer sensor edge at 0.044 m) still loses the tape at about 0.0565 m offset, and that the off-track limit of 0.06 m is a hard floor for any body width. Reach is therefore set by outer sensor x plus footprint half-size, plus tape half-width. Next, test the lead and the wheel track separately.
rationale: Iteration 1 widened the span to +/-0.036 m and dropped the score to 56.2 from 79.6. Line loss still happens once per run, and max_error still sits at about 0.061 m, the 0.06 m off-track floor. The geometry explains this. The tape is 25 mm wide, so its edge is 12.5 mm from its centre. With 16 mm footprints on the outermost sensors at x = +/-0.036 m, the outer footprint edge is at 0.044 m, so the line is lost once the tape centre is beyond about 0.0565 m. That matches the observed failure. Widening to +/-0.040 m would only push the loss point to about 0.0605 m, which is marginal. Body width cannot help, because the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and that stays at 0.06 for any body up to 0.19 m. The change is to widen the outer sensors to x = +/-0.060 m, so the tape stays in view to about 0.080 m offset. I am using 7 sensors at 20 mm spacing with 16 mm footprints, so the signal stays smooth and the centre resolution is kept. I am also keeping wheel_track 0.10 m and mass 0.8 kg, so this iteration tests sensing reach alone. Expected result: line_loss_events drop to 0, max_error falls below 0.06 m, and progress on the s-bend and slalom rises well above iteration 1. Risk: the wider 7-sensor span may add steering_oscillation, since the signal is now more sensitive to edge crossings.
